messages:
Dmitri: Heads-up — new external candidate landed: QueryFlux-7B (opt repo). Asking for quick intake: quant experiments, smoke evals, rough cost/latency estimate. Can we slot this for next sprint prioritization?
Maya: I can run basic quant experiments (awq/int8) and a small eval sweep. ETA ~48h.
Lucas: Product: curious about few-shot RAG quality vs current Atlas model. If QF-7B improves end-user accuracy by >3% on our app prompts, we should fast-track.
Joan: Is there any red-flag license or data requirement? If private data needed then Private deployment might be required.
Dmitri: License is Apache-2 from vendor, no extra TOU. Good candidate for hosted + dedicated later.
Maya: Quick plan: 1) int8/awq quant smoke 2) eval on our 1000 prompt benchmark (QA/conciseness/ hallucination) 3) perf bench on p4d-like instance.
Maya: Running command now: ```awq quantize --model queryflux-7b --bits 8 --out ./qf7b_int8```
EvalBot: Started job qf7b-smoke-001 — will post results to https://dash.redwood.ai/evals/qf7b-smoke once done.
Sam: For perf, what target SLOs should we measure? 95p latency, tokens/sec?
Dmitri: Target: 95p < 120ms for 512-token context on a0-class instance. Also log memory for KV cache to estimate cost.
Lucas: Also request a product-focused quality delta: run A/B on 200 real user prompts (anonymized) to estimate false-positive hallucination rate.
Maya: Noted. Prioritization ask: where do we place this on intake rubric? I think scoring: novelty=3, infra-risk=2, user-impact=4, work-est=2 => total 11 (we use 15-scale). Thoughts?
Joan: That feels medium-high. If quant quality is solid, raises to high.
Sam: Capacity note: if we plan to serve hosted, we need an extra p4 pool slot during canary. +1 engineer ops time to add monitoring.
Dmitri: Proposed next steps: - Maya runs quant + smoke eval (48h) - EvalBot posts results - Lucas/Joan run product A/B (2 days) - Sam preps canary pool (on-demand)
Lucas: I'll prep canary criteria: accuracy delta, latency, cost-per-request.
Maya: Quick interim numbers from first int8 run: MMLU macro ~58.9 (baseline fp16 60.1), avg latency 92ms @ batch1, memory 14GB. Posting full logs in 2h.
Dmitri: Good early signal. Slight MMLU drop but within acceptable threshold for many use-cases.
Joan: If hallucination rate on the 200 user prompts is <2% we can move to canary.
EvalBot: qf7b-smoke-001 completed — results: 1) MMLU 58.9 2) Rouge-L small drop 3) hallucination approx 2.7% on synthetic set. Full report: https://dash.redwood.ai/evals/qf7b-smoke/results
Maya: Uploading quant artifacts to s3: s3://redwood-onboard/queryflux/1715554321/
Sam: I'll schedule a 24h canary capacity; tagging infra-oncall. If canary looks good we can flip dedicated routing.
Dmitri: Okay, decision point scheduled for tomorrow 10am sync. Can everyone react with :thumbsup: if they can attend?
Maya: :thumbsup:
Lucas: :thumbsup:
Joan: :thumbsup:
Sam: :thumbsup:
Dmitri: Thanks — summary pinned: 1) run full eval + A/B, 2) quantify cost/latency, 3) prepare canary. If product gains >3% or hallucinations <=2% we prioritize for next sprint.
Lucas: Added a short note to roadmap board: https://roadmap.redwood.ai/board#queryflux (ETA gating decision next week).
Maya: Will post final numbers here when quant artifacts and evals done.
EvalBot: Reminder: eval retention policy will archive raw traces in 7 days unless flagged.
Dmitri: Cool — closing intake thread for now, will re-open with final results.
